observation_summary: The command-line flag '--process_closure_primitives' could not be set to false because the compiler options were only updated when the flag was true, leaving the default value (true) in place even when the user explicitly requested false.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces a conditional 'if' block that only set the option to 'true' with a direct assignment of the flag's value to the option. This is a classic case of incorrect initialization/assignment logic where the state was not being correctly synchronized with the user-provided configuration.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'Flag can't be set to false due to a missing "else" in the command-line parser.'
The fix diff shows: '- if (flags.process_closure_primitives) { options.closurePass = true; }' replaced by '+ options.closurePass = flags.process_closure_primitives;'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the original code used an 'if' statement, the root cause is not a missing guard or validation, but rather the failure to correctly assign the intended value to the configuration object.
The fix is a simple assignment correction, not a rewrite of a complex procedure or algorithm.
